learning_outcomes.text: The student has insight into the functioning of a programmable system (number systems, processing of variables and constants, ASCII codes…)
The student has insight into the functioning of I/O in a computer system (LCD, PIO, SIO, time adjustment, controlling I/O applications,…)
The student converts a generic task into a methodical solution using a microcontroller.
The student independently processes provided information about microcontrollers, including manufacturer documentation.
The student creates flowcharts for microcontrollers.
The student uses the basic structure of the microcontroller to create a usable program.
The student masters machine language and associated programming techniques.
The student uses an IDE in machine language.
The student is able to let the microcontroller exchange information with the outside world, based on a fundamental, thorough and practical knowledge of the available periphery and interface.

syllabus_topics: Standard I/O (PIO, SIO, ADC, PWM, timers, interrupt,...) and its use.
Interface (LCD, dipswitch, LED, motors) and its use.
Use of an IDE in machine language.
Basic programming techniques in machine language.
assessment_rules: The assessment takes place during a practical exam. It is an open book exam where students can use all available material individually to solve a practical problem. Aids that enable communication with third parties (laptop, internet, smartphone, etc.) are NOT allowed. The theory is implicitly evaluated during the open book exam. For resits, partial transfers are available for successful partial results of 'Embedded Fundamentals: Theory' and 'Embedded Fundamentals: Lab' (within the academic year). The resit follows the same modalities as the first examination opportunity.
